_README: Overload resolution table for `torch.<op>(...)`.
Each key is a name `torch/__init__.py` hoists off `_C._VariableFunctions`.
Each value is the ordered list of aten schemas that torch's *Python*
binding exposes under that name -- not every aten overload of that name.
The distinction is load-bearing: `aten::pow` has fifteen overloads, of
which eleven (`pow.int`, `pow.float_complex`, `pow.Scalar_Scalar`, ...)
are TorchScript numeric builtins that `torch.pow` will not accept, and
listing them would make `torch.pow(2, 3)` return a float where real torch
raises TypeError.
ORDER IS THE ALGORITHM. The resolver takes the first schema that binds,
exactly as `PythonArgParser::raw_parse` does, so the order here is not
cosmetic. Two places where a plausible order is the wrong one, both
measured against torch 2.13.0 with a `TorchDispatchMode` logger rather
than reasoned about (docs/OVERLOAD.md §3):
* `.out` variants come first. They take `out` as a required kwarg-only
argument, so they bind only when the caller passed `out=`, and putting
them last would let the non-out schema swallow the call and drop the
output tensor on the floor.
* `arange.start` comes before `arange.start_step`, even though
`start_step`'s `step=1` default makes it bind a two-argument call too.
Real torch sends `torch.arange(0, 5)` to `arange.start`, and reversing
these two would name the wrong key in the work queue.
Provenance: the schema strings are `str(torch.ops.aten.<op>.<ov>._schema)`
from torch 2.13.0, transcribed here. Unlike `surface.json` this could not
come from the vendored tree -- see docs/OVERLOAD.md §2 for what the tree
does and does not carry -- so `pytests/verify_schemas.py` re-derives them
from upstream and diffs, which keeps the table from drifting silently.
That script needs real torch; the build does not.
Notes on the entries docs/NN_SURFACE.md added, where the reason is not
self-evident:
* `where` -- `.self_out` first, per the `.out` rule above. The scalar
mixes cannot shadow each other (`ScalarSelf` needs a scalar in the
second slot, `ScalarOther` in the third), so their relative order is
cosmetic, but it follows the vendored `.pyi` declaration order anyway.
The bare `where(Tensor condition) -> Tensor[]` goes last: it is the
`nonzero`-shaped overload and binds one argument, which nothing else
does.
* `bmm` carries `.dtype`/`.dtype_out` because the vendored
`_VariableFunctions.pyi` really does expose an `out_dtype` parameter.
Leaving them out would make `torch.bmm(a, b, out_dtype=...)` report
'no matching overload' where upstream accepts it.
* `rsub` is here rather than in `methods.json` because that is the route
the vendored tree takes: `torch/_tensor.py:1108` spells `Tensor.
__rsub__` as `_C._VariableFunctions.rsub(self, other)`. `1 - x` is
measured 8 times in a Llama `generate` (docs/NN_SURFACE.md §3).
Three names a model path calls are deliberately NOT here, because they
are `CompositeImplicitAutograd` upstream and an overload entry would
invent a kernel requirement upstream does not have: `linear`, `dropout`,
and `layer_norm`. All three are Python-level compositions in
`bootstrap.py` (`_install_nn`, `_install_composites`), and all three
still end at `_C._aten_dispatch`.
`layer_norm` specifically: `torch.ops.aten.layer_norm.default` exists as
a schema, but a `TorchDispatchMode` logger on torch 2.13.0 never sees it
fire -- `F.layer_norm`, `torch.layer_norm` and `nn.LayerNorm` all bottom
out at `aten.native_layer_norm.default` only, because `layer_norm` is a
thin C++ wrapper that calls `native_layer_norm` and keeps the first of
its three results. Listing `aten::layer_norm(...)` here would resolve
correctly and then name a kernel this shim will never implement, where
the honest key is one it already has -- same shape of problem as
`methods.json`'s `softmax` note. `native_layer_norm` itself has no such
mismatch (it *is* the leaf op), so it gets a normal entry above.
`split` above lists only `split.Tensor` (the int-size overload), not the
full `torch.ops.aten.split.*` overload set. That is deliberate and
different from `methods.json`'s `split`, which lists both `split.Tensor`
and `split_with_sizes`: `_VariableFunctions.split` (`torch._VF.split`)
is, measured, only ever called by the vendored tree with an int --
`torch/_tensor.py:Tensor.split` is what looks at the argument type and
routes a list/tuple to `torch._VF.split_with_sizes` instead, which is
why that op gets its own `split_with_sizes` key rather than being folded
in here.
`index_put_` is deliberately NOT here either, for a different reason than
`linear`/`dropout`/`layer_norm` above: `aten::index_put_`'s `indices`
argument has type `Tensor?[]` (a list of optional Tensors, one per axis),
which `_decompose_type` cannot represent -- its docstring says `?` binds
outermost, so it handles `int[]?` (an optional list) but not `Tensor?[]`
(a list of optionals). Adding this entry makes `import _C` raise at
install time (`_SCHEMA_BASE_TYPES` has no 'Tensor?' member), not merely
resolve wrong -- measured. `torch.index_put_`/`Tensor.index_put_` are
both Python-level compositions in `bootstrap.py` (`_install_composites`,
`_install_tensor_index_put_`) that dispatch straight to
`aten.index_put_.default` with no table involved, docs/SPELLINGS.md §8.2.
docs/SPELLINGS.md §6 notes on `any`/`div`/`mean`/`sum`, measured with a
`TorchDispatchMode` logger on torch 2.13.0 rather than reasoned about:
* `any` -- the `.out` group's internal order is not the same as the
non-`.out` group's. `any(x, out=o)` (no `dim`) resolves to
`any.all_out`, not `any.dims_out`, even though `dims_out`'s `dim`
parameter is also optional and would otherwise shadow it -- `all_out`
simply comes first in the declaration order the real arg parser
tries. `any.dims_out`/`any.out` follow, keyed off `dim` being a
list/tuple versus a plain `int`, mirroring the non-`.out` group below.
* `sum` -- `aten::sum.out` (the no-`dim` `.out` overload) is listed in
`torch.ops.aten.sum.overloads()` but **`torch.sum` never reaches
it**: `torch.sum(x, out=o)` raises `TypeError` from the real arg
parser before any dispatch happens, because the no-`dim` Python
overload plainly does not accept `out=`. `sum.out` is left out of
this table for that reason -- listing it would name a path upstream
itself does not expose, the same complaint `layer_norm` above makes
about a schema that resolves to a kernel this shim will never reach.
`mean` does not have this gap -- `mean(x, out=o)` (no `dim`) resolves
to `mean.dtype_out`, a real reachable overload -- so `mean` lists all
four.
`transpose`, `permute` and `sub` came from docs/DECOMP.md §4: they are
not names a model path calls, they are names *upstream's own
decomposition rules* call while the decomposition pass runs them. The
rule for `aten.t.default` calls `torch.transpose`, the rule for
`aten.transpose.int` calls `torch.permute`, and the rule for
`aten.rsub.Scalar` calls `torch.sub`. Every one of the three names an
aten key this shim already implements, so the entry is the whole fix --
no kernel is invented. `sub` mirrors `add` above and omits
`sub.Scalar_out` for the same reason `add` omits `add.Scalar_out`.
`log` (docs/ARCH20.md §4) is the second op after `pow` where the
`aten::` packet is mostly TorchScript numerics, and it is a sharper
case: **fourteen of `aten::log`'s sixteen overloads are scalar
builtins** (`log.int`, `log.float`, `log.Scalar`, `log.int_float`,
`log.complex_complex`, ...), and `torch.log` accepts none of them --
`torch.log(2.0)` is a TypeError from the arg parser upstream. Only the
two `Tensor` schemas are listed, and the `.out` one comes first per the
rule above. Listing the numerics would turn a call upstream refuses into
a call this shim answers, which is the divergence direction that costs
the most to find. `exp`, added in the same round for `mamba`, has the
same shape (four of its overloads are numerics) and gets the same
treatment; both kernels already existed, so both entries are the whole
fix.
`stack` (cohere, docs/ARCH20.md §5) had a kernel and no spelling --
`aten.stack.default` has been in `IMPLEMENTED` and golden-compared since
docs/ARCH.md, and `torch.stack(...)` still refused. That is the pattern
the coverage sweep is structurally unable to see: it traces on upstream
and asks whether every *dispatched* operator is implemented here, so a
missing `torch.<name>` never appears in it.
`constant_pad_nd` (bert, §2) is the reverse -- a genuinely new kernel.
Its `.out` sibling is omitted for the reason `sum.out` is: this shim has
no out-variant kernel, and `F.pad` never asks for one.
docs/ARCH20.md §9's 25-name inventory (docs/SPELLINGS.md has the full
per-name accounting): 22 got a `torch.<name>` entry here, 3
(`gelu`/`silu`/`softplus`) did not -- measured against torch 2.13.0,
`hasattr(torch, 'gelu')` is `False`. There is no `torch.gelu` upstream,
only `torch.nn.functional.gelu` / `torch._C._nn.gelu`, both of which
this shim already answers (`bootstrap.py`'s `_install_nn`). Adding a
`torch.gelu` entry here would invent a spelling upstream itself does
not have -- the same complaint `layer_norm` above makes, from the other
direction. `scalar_tensor` and `convolution` were checked the same way
and both *do* have a bare `torch.<name>`, so both get an entry despite
being the two lowest-level names on the list.
`.out` variants are omitted from every one of the 22 for the reason
`sum.out`/`constant_pad_nd.out` above are: none of the twenty-two
kernels has an out-variant, and `torch.<name>(..., out=)` is not a
call any measured caller makes for these names.
`clamp` and `min` each list a schema with no kernel behind it, in the
Tensor-first order `methods.json`'s own `clamp`/`min` entries already
use -- mirrored rather than re-decided, so the two tables agree on the
same op. Measured (`TorchDispatchMode`, torch 2.13.0):
`torch.clamp(x, min=t)` (a Tensor bound) resolves `clamp.Tensor`,
`torch.clamp(x, min=1.0)` and `torch.clamp(x)` (neither given) both
resolve `clamp.default`/`clamp.Tensor` respectively and this shim has a
kernel only for the Scalar form (`aten.clamp.default`) -- `clamp.Tensor`
names a work item, same as `methods.json` already documents for it.
`min.other` and `min.dim` were the sharper case and are no longer:
docs/SPELLINGS.md §7.2 listed both here with *no* kernel behind either,
as a precise work item for whoever owned `aten.rs` next. That work item
is closed -- docs/TRIL.md §3 implemented both, as the `min` half of one
`extremum_dim`/`extremum_other` shared with `max`, and both are in
`_aten_implemented()` with golden case builders. All four of
`max`/`min` x `.dim`/`.other` now compute. **Re-read this note before
trusting it**: it named a gap for one round after that gap moved, which
is the failure mode this repository keeps hitting with refusal text.
`max`'s two-tensor overload is the one name here where the schema
listed is not the one upstream's *own* dispatcher shows for that call.
Measured: `torch.max(a, b)` (two Tensors) fires `aten::maximum`, not
`aten::max.other` -- `max.other` is native_functions.yaml's own
comment calls it, verbatim, "binary max, alias of maximum", and this
shim has no `maximum` kernel at all. `max.other` is listed here anyway
because it is a real, separate ATen op (not a name this shim invents),
its kernel already exists and is mathematically the same elementwise
maximum `aten::maximum` computes, and the alternative -- leaving the
two-tensor overload out entirely -- would refuse a call this shim can
already answer correctly. This is different from the `layer_norm` case
above: there, the schema names a kernel this shim will never have;
here, the kernel exists and is checked against upstream's `torch.max`
*values*, only the internal ATen op name differs from what upstream's
own dispatcher happens to pick.
`mul.Scalar` mirrors the `div_.Scalar`/`add_.Scalar` divergence already
documented above, on the non-in-place side this time: measured,
`torch.mul(x, 2.0)` dispatches `aten::mul.Tensor` (upstream's own `.pyi`
even types `mul`'s `input`/`other` as `Tensor | Number`, wrapping the
scalar before an overload is picked), so `mul.Scalar` is listed as a
fallback that computes rather than one upstream's dispatcher is
measured to reach. `torch.mul(2.0, x)` (scalar *first*) is not
supported -- neither schema's `self` parameter accepts a bare Python
number, and no measured caller in this repository writes a function
call with the scalar in the first slot (`2.0 * x` goes through
`__rmul__`, already a `methods.json` entry).
docs/TRIL.md added `amax`, `tril` and `triu` (and the same three to
`methods.json`). All three are the `stack` pattern above -- a kernel
with no name -- but they arrived by two different routes, which is the
part worth keeping:
* `amax`'s kernel landed one round earlier as the fix for the
attention path's quadratic term (docs/SEQLEN.md §7), reachable only
as `torch.ops.aten.amax.default`. `torch.amax` and `Tensor.amax`
both refused. The golden harness compared the kernel the whole time
and could not see it, so that round left a *smoke test* pinning the
absence by name -- which is what made this a one-line fix rather
than a rediscovery. The test now pins the presence instead.
* `tril`/`triu` are new kernels. `tril` is GPT-BigCode's last wall
(docs/TORCHSCRIPT.md §6): `torch.tril(torch.ones((n, n),
dtype=torch.bool))` in `GPTBigCodeModel.__init__`. `triu` is the
mirror and falls out of the same function for a sign flip -- checked
first that `hasattr(torch, 'triu')` is `True`, the
`gelu`/`silu`/`softplus` test above, before adding a name.
`softmax` is deliberately NOT here, and it is the nearest miss in this
file. `torch.softmax(x, dim=1)` did refuse, and `aten::softmax.int` is a
real schema that would validate against upstream -- but it is
`CompositeImplicitAutograd` and a `TorchDispatchMode` logger never sees
it fire; `aten._softmax.default` is what every spelling reaches
(re-measured, docs/TRIL.md §2). The fix is a Python-level composite in
`bootstrap.py::_install_composites`, bound to `TensorBase.softmax` so
the two spellings are one function. Same reasoning as `layer_norm` and
as `methods.json`'s own `softmax` note.
`_safe_softmax` came out of the same round's audit and is the leading
underscore's own trap: the name *looks* private, so it was bucketed in
docs/ARCH20.md §9 as "no such public function upstream, or reached
another way", and both halves were wrong. `hasattr(torch,
'_safe_softmax')` is `True` on 2.13.0 and `torch._safe_softmax(x, 1)`
fires exactly one record -- `aten._safe_softmax.default`, the same key
this shim has had a golden-compared kernel for since docs/SDPA.md. It is
a leaf op, not a composite, so unlike `softmax` two entries above the
table entry *is* the right fix. No `methods.json` entry: upstream has no
`Tensor._safe_softmax` either.
That mis-bucketing is worth keeping because of what it cost. Two
refusals in `bootstrap.py`'s `scaled_dot_product_attention` named
`aten._safe_softmax.default` as a kernel that did not exist, long after
it did -- the same stale-refusal defect the bool-mask note in that
function already records against itself. A name that is never called
cannot correct the text that says it is missing.
`_log_softmax` (docs/LOSS.md) is the `_safe_softmax` shape exactly, and
the pair with `softmax` above is the reason both notes are kept: the
*public* spelling `torch.log_softmax` has parser key
`aten::log_softmax.int`, which is `CompositeImplicitAutograd` and belongs
in `bootstrap.py` next to `softmax`; the *private* spelling
`torch._log_softmax` has parser key `aten::_log_softmax`, which is the
dispatched leaf and belongs here. Two names one underscore apart, and the
right answer for each is the opposite of the right answer for the other.
